scope: Bounded recovery of Crump-to-Blyth 1819 cited by Blyth 1817; determine whether 1818 is a merged enclosure identifier. No accepted links, source edits, packet changes or exports.

source_identity.title: From Charles Wade Crump to Edward Blyth [before 8 January 1856]
source_identity.forwarding_route: The source is not addressed to Darwin. DCP 1817 says Blyth forwarded it to Darwin as a memorandum on wild cattle; this establishes a forwarding claim, not Crump's direct receipt by Darwin or a direct Crump-to-Darwin letter.

date_constraints.reason: The broad raw XML lower bound is an archival metadata artifact; the editorial date and forwarding relationship constrain it to before Blyth's 8 January 1856 letter.

source_identity.physical_description: AmemS 5pp, with CD annotation; manuscript source DAR 98: A114-A116, CUL.

full_reading.body_status: Complete 7 retained body paragraphs read. The manuscript begins with a cover/title block naming facts about lions and wild cattle, then gives Crump's wild-cattle account.
full_reading.body_summary: Crump separates hearsay from personal observation. He reports a reputed dull brick-red wild-cattle breed in Tinneyvelly, then describes an officer's account and skin/horns of a red bull near Rajas Choultry, a herd formed by the bull breeding with village cows, its alleged extermination by Kennedy, and a second grey-white lagoon cattle breed reported to him by Jerdon. The text attributes hearsay and named witnesses rather than presenting all claims as Crump observation.

exact_evidence.quote: Facts regarding Lions in Central India and Wild Cattle in Southern India | Chas Crump. | Artillery
So much I know only by hearsay— the following is of my own knowledge
from this intercourse in process of time sprung calves—two at first, red like their father
I have heard from Jerden of another breed of wild cattle living in the salt water lagoons and islands above Nellore

full_reading.apparatus: The only CD annotation is two scored brown-crayon marks. Footnotes identify Blyth's forwarding context, Crump's cover-note additions, and later Jerdon 1867 comparison; these later editorial references are not Crump voice.
full_reading.bibliography: No separate bibliography section is present in the recovered HTML. Footnote 8 cites Jerdon 1867, p. 301 as a later comparison, not as part of Crump's 1856 source.

visuals.note: Cambridge facsimiles show a handwritten Crump memorandum, with title 'Wild Cattle in the South', crossings/insertions, and a two-page spread. They do not show a Darwin letter or a separate 1818 document.

1818_identity_check.result: 1818 is a merged/virtual enclosure identifier, not a separate CSV/XML source in the pinned revision.
evidence: The pinned Epsilon CSV has DCP-LETT-1817 and DCP-LETT-1819 but no DCP-LETT-1818 row (apart from unrelated later IDs containing the digits 1818).
1817's HTML has one [Enclosure] section titled Notes for Mr. Darwin, with 15 transcribed paragraphs; its physical description is ALS 6pp plus an Amem 12pp enclosure.

1817's XML abstract explicitly says it encloses 'notes for Mr. D' [1818] and a memorandum on wild cattle [1819]. Thus 1818 labels the Notes for Mr. Darwin component inside the 12-page enclosure, while 1819 is the separate Crump memorandum forwarded with the same Blyth letter.
The 1819 XML itself states: [This memorandum was forwarded to CD enclosed with 1817.]

limits: The 1819 text is Crump-to-Blyth and reaches Darwin only through Blyth's claimed forwarding; no Darwin receipt or response is established here.
1818 has no independent pinned XML/CSV record in this revision; its status as the Notes for Mr. Darwin enclosure is based on 1817's explicit abstract and enclosure structure.
No acceptance or new relationship edge is proposed.
